problem:
Find the arc length of the curve $r(t)=⟨2t\operatorname{cos}⁡2t-\operatorname{sin}⁡2t,\,\frac{3{t}^{2}}{2},\,2t\operatorname{sin}⁡2t+\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩$
from  $t=0$ to $t=2.$

activity_context.topic_title: The Arc Length of a Vector-Valued Function

examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Arc Length of a Three-Dimensional Spatial Curve
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14052793/assets/8573aedcd26cba038b2db072560cd3d6ba7676542888a2d9b8a356713eaf6724.png)

Find the arc length of the curve $\mathbf r (t) = \langle \sin t ,\: \cos t, \: t \rangle$
from  $t =0$ to $t = 2\pi.$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we find $\mathbf r'(t)$ and $\|\mathbf r'(t)\|\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}+(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡t+{sin}^{2}⁡t+1} \\  & =\sqrt{1+1} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the arc length of the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\sqrt{2}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\text{ }\sqrt{2}\,t{|}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =\sqrt{2}(2\pi -0) \\  & =2\sqrt{2}\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Find the arc length of the curve $g(t)=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡t-\frac{{t}^{2}}{2},\,2t⟩$ from $t=1$ to $t=e.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find ${g}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{g}^{′}(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t-\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{t}-t,\,2⟩ \\ ‖{g}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{t}-t)}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}-2+{t}^{2}+4} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}+2+{t}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{t}+t)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{t}+t\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the arc length of the curve is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{1}^{e}‖{g}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{e}(\frac{1}{t}+t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡t+\frac{{t}^{2}}{2}){|}_{1}^{e} \\  & =(\operatorname{ln}⁡e+\frac{{e}^{2}}{2})-(\operatorname{ln}⁡1+\frac{{1}^{2}}{2}) \\  & =1+\frac{{e}^{2}}{2}-0-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2}+1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
